text: dsh-llm-kiro 是适用于 DSH 的 AWS Kiro 模型提供方插件，将已登录的 Kiro 账户接入 kiro 模型路由。它向 DSH 注册 LLM 适配器，并把对话请求发送到 Kiro，支持 Claude 和开放权重模型、流式响应、推理内容映射、可配置模型目录与重试策略。代理、区域和模型参数可按设置调整，设置变更可用于后续请求。适合希望通过已有 Kiro 登录在 DSH 中使用这些模型的用户；需要本机 Kiro IDE 或 kiro-cli 登录，Claude 模型还可能需要获准的网络出口。

dsh-llm-kiro connects an AWS Kiro sign-in to DSH as a model provider. It supports Claude and open-weight models, streams responses, and accepts configurable model and proxy settings. Use it to access Kiro models in DSH; Kiro IDE or kiro-cli sign-in is required, and Claude may need permitted egress.
想用已经登录的 Kiro 账号给 DSH 提供 Claude 模型。
让 DSH 可以通过 Kiro 调用 DeepSeek、GLM 或 Qwen 这类模型。
我想在 DSH 里切换到 Kiro 提供的模型路由。
能不能让 DSH 把模型回复作为流式内容接收？
希望根据 Kiro 账号的网络出口配置 Claude 请求代理。
有没有办法让已登录的 Kiro 凭据自动用于 DSH，而不用另存一份密钥？
Can I use my existing Kiro sign-in to access Claude models in DSH?
I want DSH to stream responses from models available through Kiro.
dsh-llm-kiro 的功能「Kiro 模型提供方」：将 kiro 路由注册到 DSH，并列出可选模型。发起对话时选择提供方和模型，未列入目录的模型 ID 也会传给服务。
dsh-llm-kiro 的功能「流式模型响应」：把 Kiro 返回的数据流转换为 DSH 的流式内容，并处理取消、空闲超时和传输异常。由一次模型请求触发，结果作为文本等响应块输出。
dsh-llm-kiro 的功能「配置模型请求」：通过 llm-kiro 设置指定区域、代理、思考选项、模型目录和超时策略。用户更新设置后，后续请求会读取新的连接参数。
dsh-llm-kiro 的功能「Kiro 凭据读取」：请求时读取 Kiro IDE 或 CLI 保存的令牌，并在令牌临近过期时刷新；令牌缓存留在内存中，不要求另行配置 API key。
dsh-llm-kiro 使用前须知：需要先在本机通过 Kiro IDE 或 kiro-cli 登录；插件从 Kiro 管理的 SSO 缓存读取凭据。（见 src/auth.ts:108-115）

dsh-llm-kiro README · dsh-llm-kiro：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

An [AWS Kiro](https://kiro.dev) (CodeWhisperer) adapter for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) LLM seam. It registers the `kiro` provider route, so a signed-in Kiro account serves Claude and open-weight models to the harness without a separate API key.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Requirements：- A working `dsh` install (this package is a plugin, not a standalone tool).
- A Kiro sign-in on the same machine. The Kiro IDE or `kiro-cli` writes the tokens this adapter reads; it never stores a second copy of the credential.
- For Claude models: a permitted network egress. See [Why Claude needs a proxy](#why-claude-needs-a-proxy).

dsh-llm-kiro README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:caopu16/dsh-llm-kiro
```

That is the whole install, and upgrading is the same command again. Built `lib/` is committed to the repository precisely so a git-sourced install runs no build script: pnpm 10 and later block dependency build scripts until each is allowlisted by a key carrying its resolved commit, which would make every upgrade a manual allowlist edit.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Install：The package declares its own patch layer, so installing it mounts the adapter — no `cordis.yml` editing required to make the route exist. Add configuration only for the facts this package deliberately leaves empty.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Without the `dsh` command：`dsh` on PATH comes from an installed `@deepseek-ai/dsh`. When you are working from a harness source checkout instead, run the CLI from that checkout and every command above works unchanged:

```sh
cd /path/to/deepseek-harness
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add github:caopu16/dsh-llm-kiro
pnpm dsh --profile web
```

A source checkout requires `pnpm run build` first, since the profile loads built `lib/` rather than TypeScript sources.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Developing this plugin：`lib/` is committed, so a change to `src/` reaches consumers only after it is rebuilt and committed too:

```sh
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

dsh-llm-kiro README · Configure：Kiro authorizes Claude models by request egress, and the permitted egress differs per deployment, so no proxy is shipped as a default. Put yours in the `llm-kiro:` section of `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` (`~/.dsh/settings.yaml`):

```yaml
llm-kiro:
  proxyUrl: http://proxy.example:1082
  reasoningEffort: medium
```

dsh-llm-kiro README · Configure：This is the recommended home for every field below. The plugin registers `llm-kiro` as a settings namespace, so the section reloads without a restart, it outranks the composition entry, and it is what the web Models page writes.

Note that `--dump-config` prints the composition tree only, so a field configured here does not appear there. To confirm the proxy is in use, ask a `claude-*` model something: without a permitted egress it fails with `INVALID_MODEL`.

Every field is optional:

dsh-llm-kiro README · Configure：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `proxyUrl` | none (direct) | Egress for every Kiro request, `http://` or `https://`, with optional `user:pass@`. An invalid value fails plugin loading. |
| `region` | the signed-in token's region | Selects the `q.<region>.amazonaws.com` endpoint. |
| `profileArn` | the signed-in client's own ARN | CodeWhisperer profile the account bills against; discovered from Kiro's `profile.json`, so set this only to override it. |
| `thinking` | `enabled` | `disabled` locks every request to effort `off`. |
| `reasoningEffort` | `off` | `off`, `low`, `medium`, or `high`. |
| `defaultContextWindow` | `200000` | Capacity used for a model with no exact value. |
| `models` | the verified account tier | Advisory catalog for model selectors; unlisted ids still reach the wire. |
| `streamIdleTimeoutMs` | `300000` | Maximum provider idle time while one read is outstanding. |
| `tokenExpiryBufferMs` | `300000` | Refresh the access token this long before expiry. |
| `retryPolicy` | bounded normal | Provider-owned retry policy, executed by `dsh-llm-retry`. |

dsh-llm-kiro README · Configuring in the profile instead：A deployment that wants the proxy pinned to one profile, rather than to the machine, can patch the row in `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/cordis.patch.yml` instead:

```yaml
- id: llm-kiro
  config:
    proxyUrl: http://proxy.example:1082
```

dsh-llm-kiro README · Configuring in the profile instead：Two cautions. The entry targets the existing row **by id** — do not wrap it in an `insert:` list, because this package's own patch layer already inserts `llm-kiro`, and a second insert of the same id fails the whole profile at boot with `duplicate loader entry id: llm-kiro`. And a patch layer only takes effect on restart, whereas the settings section reloads live.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Configuring in the profile instead：Configure any one field in one place. A field set in both is not an error — the settings section simply wins — but changing the patch layer then appears to do nothing.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Use：Select provider `kiro` and any model id it serves:

```
claude-opus-5     claude-opus-4.8    claude-opus-4.7   claude-opus-4.6  claude-opus-4.6-1m
claude-opus-4.5   claude-sonnet-5    claude-sonnet-4.6 claude-sonnet-4.6-1m
claude-sonnet-4.5 claude-sonnet-4    claude-haiku-4.5  auto
deepseek-3.2      glm-5              minimax-m2.5      qwen3-coder-next

dsh-llm-kiro README · Use：Model ids are passed through as the wire `modelId`, so a model Kiro adds later works without upgrading this package. The shipped catalog is advisory only: an unlisted id still reaches the service, and the ids above are the ones one account tier was observed to accept. `minimax-m2.1` is omitted because the service reports it temporarily unavailable, and the `-1m` variants of Sonnet 4.5, Sonnet 5, and Opus 4.8 because it rejects them as unknown — another tier may differ.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Why Claude needs a proxy：Kiro authorizes model families by request egress, not only by account entitlement. From an unauthorized egress every `claude-*` id is refused with `INVALID_MODEL` while the open-weight ids answer normally; through a permitted egress the same account and token reach the whole catalog. `proxyUrl` therefore exists for correctness, not performance, and the open-weight models need no proxy at all.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Why Claude needs a proxy：The proxy is opened as an HTTP `CONNECT` tunnel with TLS negotiated inside it, so the proxy sees only the target host name, never request contents or the bearer token.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Credentials：The adapter reads `~/.aws/sso/cache/kiro-auth-token.json` plus the sibling device-registration file it names. When the stored access token is still valid it is used as-is; otherwise the adapter exchanges the refresh token for a fresh one and caches that **in memory only**. Kiro owns those files and writes them from its own sign-in, so writing back would race a process this plugin does not coordinate with.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Credentials：The profile ARN is discovered the same way, from the `profile.json` the signed-in Kiro client writes under its `globalStorage` (`~/.kiro-server/data/User/globalStorage/kiro.kiroagent/`, then `~/.kiro/...`). This is required rather than convenient: an IdC or Enterprise account has no implicit default profile, and a request naming none is refused with 403 `User is not authorized to make this call.` A personal account needs no profile, so a missing or malformed file is not an error — the request simply carries none. Configuration outranks discovery: set `profileArn` only to override it.
dsh-llm-kiro README · Credentials：A missing sign-in fails the first request with `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` naming the expected path, rather than failing at load or silently producing nothing.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Kiro request：**What the model sees.** Kiro has no system slot, so the harness system prompt is prepended to the earliest user turn, where thinking markers also go. History is folded into the strict user/assistant alternation the service requires; a gap becomes a `[system: conversation continues]` placeholder. Tool schemas ride on the current turn. A tool result whose issuing call is absent from history (compaction dropped it) is carried as text, because the service rejects the unmatched id.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Kiro request：**Token effect.** Provider tokenization governs exact input. The thinking markers add a fixed short prefix at any effort above `off`; placeholders add a few tokens per gap.

**KV Cache effect.** Kiro assigns a fresh `conversationId` per request and this adapter does not replay provider-side conversation state, so cache reuse is the service's own concern. Keeping the system prompt on the earliest turn preserves a stable prefix.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Kiro response：**What the model sees.** The response is a `vnd.amazon.eventstream` frame sequence. Text and thinking share one channel delimited by `<thinking>` markers; the adapter routes them into harness text and reasoning blocks, holding back only a tail short enough to be a partial marker so a marker split across frames is still recognized. The open-weight routes additionally leak a `<｜DSML｜` tool-call preamble into that channel, which is suppressed as a prompt-format artifact.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Kiro response：**Token effect.** Kiro reports context occupancy, not token counts: each response stream ends with a `contextUsageEvent` carrying the percentage of the model's context window the request consumed, and the adapter emits it as a `usage` chunk by multiplying that percentage by the model's window. Output tokens and cache splits are not reported and are counted as zero.

**KV Cache effect.** Loop-retained blocks append to the next request like any other adapter's.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Errors：`AUTH` (401, or a 403 naming an invalid bearer token), `FORBIDDEN` (other 403s, including an unentitled subscription), `RATE_LIMIT` (429), `INVALID_MODEL` (a 400 whose body names `INVALID_MODEL_ID` — usually an unauthorized egress), `INVALID_REQUEST` (other 400s), `SERVER` (5xx). Transport failures throw `TRANSPORT` naming the target host; caller aborts throw `ABORTED`. Protocol violations raise `STREAM_CLOSED` (a stream ending mid-frame) or `MALFORMED_RESPONSE` (a bad frame header or payload). A stream that completes with no content at all finishes as `EMPTY_RESPONSE`.

dsh-llm-kiro README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Coarse token usage.** Kiro reports only the percentage of the context window a request consumed, so the emitted `usage` chunk carries the derived input count and a zero output count: pressure tracking is accurate, billing-style breakdowns are not.
- **No image input.** Image content is refused with `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT` rather than silently flattened, though the wire operation does accept images.
- **Tool names must match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`.** A name that does not is aliased by replacing every illegal character with `_` (so `mcp__a-b__c-d` goes on the wire as `mcp__a_b__c_d`) and reversed before dispatch; only a name no alias can rescue (empty, over-long, or not starting with a letter) is refused with `UNSUPPORTED_TOOL_NAME`. Two names that alias to the same wire name in one turn collide, last one wins.
- **SOCKS proxies are unsupported.** Only `http://` and `https://` egress; a SOCKS proxy would need a dependency this package avoids.
- **Thinking effort is a prompt marker, not a request field.** The budgets are fixed per effort level and the service may ignore them.
